record.context_brief: Refined Torelli question for Gushel-Mukai fourfolds
record.original_question: Let X1 and X2 be Gushel-Mukai fourfolds, and suppose there is an equivalence Phi: Ku(X1) -> Ku(X2) that commutes with the degree shift functors of X1 and X2. What additional assumptions on Phi are sufficient to conclude that X1 and X2 are isomorphic?

evidence.quote: Question 6.16. Let X1 and X2 be Gushel-Mukai fourfolds. Assume that there is an equivalence Phi : Ku(X1 ) -> Ku(X2 ) which commutes with the degree shift functors of X1 and X2 . Then under which assumptions on Phi we have that X1 and X2 are isomorphic?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A Gushel–Mukai (GM) fourfold is a smooth four-dimensional intersection $X = \mathrm{Cone}(\mathrm{Gr}(2,5)) \cap Q$, where $\mathrm{Cone}(\mathrm{Gr}(2,5)) \subset \mathbb{P}^{10}$ is the projective cone over the Plücker embedding of the Grassmannian $\mathrm{Gr}(2,5) \subset \mathbb{P}^9$ and $Q \subset \mathbb{P}^{10}$ is a quadric hypersurface. Equivalently, $X$ is a smooth projective fourfold of Picard rank one, index two, and degree ten admitting an embedding $X \hookrightarrow \mathrm{Gr}(2,5)$ (ordinary case) or a finite degree-two map to $\mathrm{Gr}(2,5)$ (special case).

Let $\mathcal{O}_X$ denote the structure sheaf and $\mathcal{U}_X$ the rank-two tautological subbundle pulled back from $\mathrm{Gr}(2,5)$. The bounded derived category of coherent sheaves $D^b(X)$ admits a semiorthogonal decomposition
$$D^b(X) = \langle \mathrm{Ku}(X),\, \mathcal{O}_X,\, \mathcal{U}_X^{\vee},\, \mathcal{O}_X(1),\, \mathcal{U}_X^{\vee}(1) \rangle,$$
where the Kuznetsov component $\mathrm{Ku}(X)$ is a non-commutative K3 category (its Serre functor is the shift $[2]$ and its Hochschild homology agrees with that of a K3 surface).

The degree shift functor of $X$ is the autoequivalence $\sigma_X : \mathrm{Ku}(X) \to \mathrm{Ku}(X)$ obtained as the composition of the spherical twist along a natural spherical functor with tensoring by $\mathcal{O}_X(1)$ (equivalently, the restriction to $\mathrm{Ku}(X)$ of the rotation autoequivalence associated to the Lefschetz decomposition above).

Problem. Let $X_1$ and $X_2$ be Gushel–Mukai fourfolds and let
$$\Phi : \mathrm{Ku}(X_1) \xrightarrow{\sim} \mathrm{Ku}(X_2)$$
be a $\mathbb{C}$-linear exact equivalence such that $\Phi \circ \sigma_{X_1} \cong \sigma_{X_2} \circ \Phi$. Determine sufficient conditions on $\Phi$ (for instance, conditions on the induced map on numerical/Mukai lattices, on Bridgeland stability data, on Hodge structures, or further compatibility constraints) ensuring that $X_1 \cong X_2$ as algebraic varieties.
artifact.status_search_result: Categorical Torelli-type questions for Gushel–Mukai fourfolds remain an active research topic. Surveys on categorical Torelli theorems list the problem as open, and unlike the cubic fourfold case (where compatibility with the degree shift functor suffices for a categorical Torelli result), for GM fourfolds the situation is subtler: Hodge-association is known to be strictly stronger than homological association, so a precise sufficient condition on $\Phi$ guaranteeing isomorphism of GM fourfolds has not been established.

status_evidence.title: Categorical Torelli theorems: results and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing categorical Torelli problems for GM fourfolds among open questions, contrasting with the cubic fourfold case where the degree shift functor compatibility yields a Torelli theorem.
status_evidence.claim: The refined categorical Torelli question for GM fourfolds with degree-shift-compatible equivalences is recorded as open.

status_evidence.title: Equivalence between Kuznetsov components of cubic fourfolds and Gushel-Mukai fourfolds
status_evidence.snippet: For GM fourfolds, Hodge-association of a K3 strictly implies homological association, indicating a gap between equivalences of Kuznetsov components and isomorphism of varieties.
status_evidence.claim: There is no known sufficient condition matching the cubic fourfold case for GM fourfolds.
